newsitem.title: QATAR: TENNIS-BRITAIN'S HENMAN REACHES HIS FIRST FINAL.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-BRITAIN'S HENMAN REACHES HIS FIRST FINAL.

text.p: Britain's Tim Henman reached the first final of his blossoming career on Saturday when he defeated Morocco's Hicham Arazi in the $635,000 Qatar Open.
Henman, ranked 29 in the world, beat number 78 Arazi 6-3 2-6 6-2 in 84 minutes.
The match was Henman's eighth semifinal, all of them having come in the last 11 months.
Henman wrapped up the first set in 29 minutes. He broke the Moroccan in the sixth game to lead 4-2 when Arazi hit a careless double fault.
But the Moroccan, appearing in his first semifinal, hit back in the second set, breaking Henman in the sixth and eighth games.
The British player, however, broke in the first and seventh games of the deciding set, winning the crucial final game to love when Arazi hit a return wide.
"It wasn't some of the best tennis I have ever played," said Henman, who added the windy conditions inside centre court made it difficult for both players.
"But I served well and came forward on the important points. In the second set, he hit a lot of good winners and things turned round very quickly," he said.

"But at the start of the third set, I started to slow things down. I broke his serve in the first game, and then I never looked back," said Henman, adding he would not make any special preparations for the final against American Jim Courier on Sunday.
"I will just concentrate on my own game but I think I have a chance. Fatigue won't be a problem for me and I will be fresh for the match."
"During the second set today, I was getting a little frustrated but I try not to let it show. I try to be in control of my emotions on court because that's when I play my best tennis."
Courier won his semifinal against Sergi Bruguera of Spain 6-4 6-2.
